stories.head: Salesforce to Acquire Voice AI Provider Cresta for ~$2.7 Billion
stories.plain: Salesforce is buying Cresta, which runs voice AI agents and real-time coaching for phone reps, for a reported $2.7 billion. It plugs a gap in Service Cloud — phone-based service — and signals that the platform wars for agentic CX are moving from chat to voice. Any team evaluating enterprise CX stacks needs to factor this in.

stories.head: Cyara Launches Agentic CX Trust Platform for Real-Time AI Agent Compliance
stories.plain: Cyara's new platform gives enterprises independent, real-time proof that AI agents are behaving correctly on live customer calls — catching failures as they happen. As agentic systems handle more conversations, buyers and regulators will demand exactly this kind of third-party audit layer, making this a new category of governance tooling worth watching.

stories.head: Yext Completes Acquisition of Flamel.ai, Adding Localized Ad Execution to Agentic Platform
stories.plain: Yext has closed its purchase of Flamel.ai, which automates localized paid campaigns for franchise and multi-location brands. Folded into Yext's agentic marketing stack, it means the platform can now decide, build, and launch local ads autonomously. This reshapes how multi-location brands will buy and manage media going forward.

stories.head: Liferay Launches SEO & AEO Studio Beta to Monitor Visibility Inside AI Answer Engines
stories.plain: Liferay's new tool lets marketing teams track and improve their content's presence in both traditional search and AI-generated answers from a single dashboard. As more buyers get answers from AI engines instead of search results pages, this kind of Generative Engine Optimization tooling shifts from nice-to-have to essential for organic visibility strategy.

stories.head: Hightouch Launches Match Booster in Europe, Lifting Audience Match Rates up to 90% Without Privacy Risk
stories.plain: Hightouch expanded its Match Booster feature to five European markets, reporting 15%+ higher audience match rates on average and up to 90% in one test — all within GDPR constraints. Better match rates mean more people reached with personalized ads, and doing it without compliance risk is the key hurdle for any CDP-to-media workflow in Europe.

stories.head: Salesforce to Acquire Voice AI Provider Cresta for ~$2.7 Billion
stories.plain: Salesforce is buying Cresta, a voice AI company, for a reported $2.7 billion. Cresta adds end-to-end voice agents and real-time coaching for human reps directly into Service Cloud. This is a major platform-level move that reshapes how Salesforce competes in AI-driven customer service and signals where CX budgets are heading.

stories.head: Cyara Launches Agentic CX Trust Platform for Real-Time AI Agent Quality and Compliance
stories.plain: Cyara's new platform gives enterprises independent, real-time proof of compliance and quality for every AI or human agent conversation. It catches failures as they happen and prevents repeats. As agentic AI handles more live customer interactions, third-party oversight tools like this are becoming a procurement requirement, not a nice-to-have.

stories.head: Yext Completes Acquisition of Flamel.ai, Adding Localized Ad Execution to Agentic Platform
stories.plain: Yext has closed its purchase of Flamel.ai, which automates localized paid campaign management for franchise and multi-location brands. Plugging it into Yext's agentic platform means AI can now plan, localize, and execute paid ads autonomously at scale — a concrete example of agentic decisioning moving into media buying.

stories.head: Hightouch Launches Match Booster in Europe, Lifting Match Rates Up to 90% Without Breaking Compliance
stories.plain: Hightouch's Match Booster is now live across the UK, Germany, France, Spain, and Italy, outperforming existing onboarding providers by 15% or more on average match rates — up to 90% better in one test. Better identity resolution in privacy-strict markets directly improves personalization reach and ad targeting efficiency for European marketers.

stories.head: Liferay Launches Beta SEO & AEO Studio to Track Visibility in Both Search and AI Answer Engines
stories.plain: Liferay's new studio gives marketing teams one dashboard to monitor and improve rankings in traditional search and AI answer engines simultaneously. As more buyer journeys start inside AI tools like ChatGPT or Perplexity, tracking and optimizing for both surfaces is becoming a standard marketing operations need, not a specialist task.

themes.head: AI Agents Demand Ops Redesign, Not Just Deployment
body: Autonomous AI agents are moving from pilot projects into live marketing workflows, and the consensus is clear: dropping them into existing org charts fails. Teams must redesign decision rights, data access, and accountability structures before agents can deliver on their promise — deployment alone is not transformation.

Platforms are accelerating this pressure. Asana's agentic work management and Cyara's Agentic CX Trust Platform both assume agents will run unsupervised on consequential tasks, which means quality assurance and compliance proof must be baked into the infrastructure, not bolted on afterward. The operational debt of ignoring this is compounding fast.
ev: MarTech · Building workflows around AI agents
Agile Brand · Asana agentic work management

themes.head: The AI Proof Gap Is a Leadership Crisis
body: Most marketing teams report that AI is working — but almost none can demonstrate it with numbers their CFO or CEO will accept. The gap between perceived value and provable ROI is now the central tension in AI investment conversations, and it is eroding executive confidence at exactly the moment budgets are being set for 2027.

Two compounding problems drive this: AI surfaces patterns that still require human interpretation to mean anything actionable, and legacy dashboards were never built to attribute value to autonomous or semi-autonomous decisions. Closing the proof gap requires new measurement frameworks, not just more data — and incrementality testing before peak spend is one concrete first step.

themes.head: CX Consolidation Around Voice & Agentic AI
body: Salesforce's acquisition of Cresta and Yext's absorption of Flamel.ai are not isolated deals — they signal that the major CX platforms are racing to own every modality of customer interaction, including voice, under a single AI-orchestrated roof. A year of dealmaking is converging into a small number of dominant stacks.

The strategic logic is straightforward: as AI agents handle more live customer conversations, brands need a single system of record that can guarantee quality, compliance, and continuity across human and machine interactions. Platforms that can offer independent proof of that quality — like Cyara's new trust platform — will become mandatory infrastructure rather than optional add-ons.
ev: MarTech Series · Cyara Agentic CX Trust Platform

themes.head: Search Is Splitting Into SEO vs. AEO
body: Optimizing for AI-generated answers (AEO — Answer Engine Optimization) is diverging from traditional SEO, and the two disciplines now require different content architectures, different signals, and potentially conflicting trade-offs. Liferay's launch of a combined SEO & AEO Studio is an early indicator that vendors see this as a durable split, not a passing trend.

The danger is that brands chasing AI search rankings may hollow out the user experience that made their content credible in the first place. Winning in AI search is also not sufficient for B2B buyers, who still require trust signals, peer validation, and human sales contact before committing — meaning AEO is a top-of-funnel tactic, not a full-funnel strategy.

themes.head: Identity Resolution Under Compliance Pressure Resurfaces
body: Hightouch's European launch of Match Booster — designed to raise audience match rates without breaching privacy regulations — and the renewed emphasis on podcast retargeting's identity advantage both point to the same underlying tension: match rates collapsed after cookie deprecation, and marketers are still searching for compliant ways to rebuild them at scale.

The solutions emerging are not a return to third-party data but a deeper investment in first-party identity infrastructure and privacy-safe data collaboration. This is reshaping how data teams are structured and which vendors sit at the center of the stack — making identity resolution a board-level budget conversation, not just a technical one.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack — agents, measurement, CX platforms, search, and identity — the common bottleneck is not AI capability but the human decisions, governance structures, and proof systems needed to make that capability trustworthy and accountable.
